metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast peak values by 5–10% in such contexts.
- Underestimates true price volatility in the 10–15 day window after major spikes; adjust downward by 3–7% for high-sentiment or event-driven periods.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices; apply a 3–5% downward correction to avoid overconfidence.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after peak), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope in subsequent days by 10–15%.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overreacts to recent price movements; dampen momentum-based forecasts by 5–10% for lagged or non-event-driven periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period corrections; apply a 2–5% downward adjustment in final 5–7 days if true outcome shows downward trend.
